 Aged about 33 yrs.
 2. Narasimahaiah,

1  (By Sri. M.M. Adv., for respondent no.1)
 ORDERS ON MAIN PETITION  1. This is petition filed by the petitioner u/sec. 12 of Protection Of Women From Domestic Violence Act, 2005. 
 2. By filing this petition the petitioner has sought various reliefs fallen U/sec. 18, 20 and 22 of PWDV Act- 2005. 
 3. The format as required under the DV Act is duly filled up and the same is presented by the petitioner along with the affidavit. In the required format, the detail of the petitioners' case cannot be made out, the same can be gone through in the evidence let in by the petitioner. Hence,
before considering the reliefs sought for, it becomes just and  3  C.Misc. 130/2017 necessary to look into the case of the petitioner.
 4. The petitioner stated that the marriage between the petitioner and the respondent no.1 was an arranged marriage. During the discussion with the respondent no.1,
he told the petitioner that he is land developer and having office and Toyota Innova car, Hyundai Gets car bearing no.
KA 41 M 9546 and earning a monthly about Rs.10,00,000/-
and further he told the petitioner that he is owned one acres 28 guntas agricultural land situated at Yalachaguppe village, Tavarekere, Bengaluru South taluk and 10 acres agricultural land in Haluvagilu villae, Huttariduraga hobli, 
Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
2 Kunigal taluk, Tumkur district having own house and also having several immovable properties in and around of Bengaluru City. 
 5. The petitioner further submits that the respondent no.1 earning a monthly about Rs.10,00,000/- and the respondent no.1 is owner of the commercial property situated at old no.24/3, new no.24/3B Sreegandhakaval,
 4  C.Misc. 130/2017 Bengaluru and BBMP documents are standing in the name of the respondent no.1. From the said property the respondent no.1 receiving Rs.1,00,000/- monthly rent. 
 6. The petitioner further submits that the marriage of the petitioner with respondent no.1 was held at Sri. Yedeyuru Siddalingeshwara temple, Yediyuru on dtd: 27.11.2009. 
During the marriage ceremony, the petitioner parents has given dowry of Rs.28,00,000/- by way of cash to the respondent no.1 as per the demand of the respondents , the petitioner parents had given 780 grams of gold jewelry apart from this, 5 kg silver articles, one LCD TV and other household untensils apart from baring marriage expenses. 
Further respondent nos.2 & 3 had put forth the demands to the petitioner's parents, they must give presents to the friends and relatives of the respondent who were coming to the marriage and also transportation facility should be arranged for them. In order to fulfill the demands of the Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
3 respondents the petitioner parents had spend nearly Rs.50,00,000/- along with this the petitioners parents gave  5  C.Misc. 130/2017 a very grand and expensive silk sarees to respondents, the petitioner's parents marriage was performed in a grand manner by her parents as per the whims and fancies of the respondents . 
 7. After the marriage the petitioner went to her matrimonial home at No.2497, "D" Group Layout, Srigandha Kaval, Bengaluru-91 for few days everything's was fine. Even after 15 days of marriage, there were no signs of the respondent no.1 has live the house at morning 6.00 a.m.
and come back at 10.00 p.m., and respondent no.3 has always abusing atmosphere in the house has totally changed. All the respondents have changed their attitude towards the petitioner and they have stopped to give respect to the petitioner and they have not talked with her properly. 
The petitioner had tried have to talk with her properly. The petitioner had tried to convenience her husband i.e.,
respondent no.1, but they are all not at all showed his love and respect towards his wife and his only word was that to bring money from her parents. 
 6  C.Misc. 130/2017  8. The petitioner submits that, the respondents were ill treated the petitioner so much totally unbearable as a Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
4 dutiful wife of that particular house, even then the respondent and his family members were constantly harassed and meted out cruel treatment without any fault of the petitioner in many reasons best known to them, on many occasions the respondent was beaten up by the petitioner and caused injuries on her body on dtd:
6.10.2013.
 9. The petitioner further submits that during the course of the matrimonial life between the petitioner and respondent no.1, a female baby was born on 22.10.2010 between the spouses, the female child by name Samskruthi. 
U. The petitioner constantly being harassed by the respondent he used to assault the petitioner and caused mental and physical torture, totally unbearable and posing serious threat to her life including the minor child, this has caused a lot of mental stress and strain in the mind of the petitioner and the minor child. Day by day, the respondent  7  C.Misc. 130/2017 no.1 has increased to give harassment on the petitioner for demanding dowry the respondent no.1 was beating the petitioner from his hands mercilessly and behaved in a very inhumanly manner in front of his parents and further respondent was scolding the petitioner by including her parents in the filthiest language and was always using unparliamentary language on her family. The respondent Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
5 no.1 has stopped talking with the petitioner and he has totally neglected her and her minor female child. 
 10. The petitioner further submits that after the marriage,
the respondent staying at matrimonial home the respondent always abusing and scolding the petitioner by finding fault in each and every act of the petitioner and harassed the petitioner both mentally and physically and also beaten the petitioner several times to bring additional dowry. The respondent trying to break up the relationship of the petitioner. The respondent treating the petitioner in a humiliating manner, the petitioner by tolerating all these cruelties continued her again and again with a fond hope  8  C.Misc. 130/2017 that things would change and the respondent would mend their attitude. 
 11. The petitioner further submits that she lodged a complaint against the respondents and his family members in Cr.no.158/2014 on 13.5.2014 and same the police have filed the charge sheet against the respondent in SC no.
481/2015 offence punishable u/sec. 427, 506, 307, 498-A of IPC r/w 34 of IPC and 3 & 4 of DP Act and same is pending before the Principal, City Civil and Sessions Judge,
Bengaluru.
 12. The petitioner further submits that the respondent being a land developer and having office and Toyota Innova Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
6 Car, Hyundai Gets Car bearing no. KA 41 M 9546 and earning a monthly about Rs.10,00,000/- and further they have owned 1 acres 28 guntas situated at Yalachaguppe village, Tavarekere, Bengaluru South Taluk and 10 acres agricultural land in Haluvagilu village, Huttariduraga hobli,
Kunigal taluk, Tumkur district having own house in  9  C.Misc. 130/2017 Bengaluru and also having several immovable property in and around of Bengaluru City, the respondent no.1 earning a monthly about Rs.10,00,000/- and the respondent no.1 is owner of the commercial property situated at old no.24/3,
new no.24/3B, Sreegandhakaval, Bengaluru and BBMP documents are standing in the name of the respondent no.1.
From the said property, the respondent no.1 receiving Rs.1,00,000/- monthly rent, he has no dependent on him and he is doing luxurious life without maintaining the petitioner as a husband and therefore he is liable to pay a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- per month to the petitioner for their basic needs i.e., food, clothing, shelter, water bill, power bill,
medical expenses and other incidental expenses. Hence, this petition. 
 13. On service of notice, the respondent nos.1 to 3 have not appeared before court. Hence, they placed ex-parte. 
Thereafter, the respondent no.1 was appeared before court by filing ex-parte set aside application with vakalath through Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
7 his counsel. The said application was allowed and the order  10  C.Misc. 130/2017 of ex-parte against the respondent no.1 was set aside. 
Therefore, the respondent no.1 has filed his objections, in there he denied all allegations made by the petitioner against him. Further, the respondent no.1 submits that he is not getting any rent of Rs.1,00,000/- in the property. 
Further, the respondent is not earning a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- per month as alleged in the petition. 
Further, respondent no.1 is not working at present and earlier the respondent no.1 was working as attender in real estate office, the said office has been closed after demonetization. 
 14. It is a love marriage and marriage was performed at the temple at cost of the respondent no.1 as they are from different caste. As such giving or taking dowry does not arise. Wherein, in petitioner had started harassing the respondent no.1 and the petitioner had stopped cooking and doing household work for which, the respondent no.1 asked the mother and sister of the petitioner to quit their residence. For which, all of them used to quarrel with  11  C.Misc. 130/2017 respondent no.1 and ultimately they left the matrimonial home including the petitioner. After 6-7 months the petitioner has lodged the false complaint against the Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
8 respondents and from the date to till date the petitioner is blackmailing the respondent no.1 for wrongful gain i.e.,
Rs.25,00,000/- and a site, but the respondent no.1 did not yield to their demand as the respondent no.1 do not own any absolute property. The petitioner and her mother and sister intention is not live their husbands only name sake they married and blackmailing for money.
 15. The respondent no.1 do not have any source of income to pay any damages and maintenance. Further, the respondent never troubled the petitioner at any point of time as the petitioner is living east and the respondent is living west Bengaluru as such the getting a protection order from this court does not arise. 
 16. Further, the petitioner is earning and she is capable of take care herself as such, the petitioner is not facing any  12  C.Misc. 130/2017 financial problem as she is owning site and she is residing with her mother and sister. It is further submitted that the petitioner has taken away all her cloths in the year 2012 itself. The respondent no.1 has not tortured physically or mentally to the petitioner at any point of time as alleged in the petition. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition. 
 17. Keeping in mind the evidence given by the petitioner it becomes just and necessary to look into whether the orders required by the petitioner various reliefs which are Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
9 fallen U/Sec. 18, 20 & 22 of DV Act can be granted. 
 18 . The petitioner in support of her case has got examined herself as PW.1 and got exhibited documents as Exs.P.1 to 24. Ex. P.1 is marriage invitation , Exs.P.2 & 3 are certified copies of sale deed dtd: 04.09.2014, Exs.P.4 & 5 are encumbrance certificates, Exs.P.6 to 14 are RTC extracts,
Ex.P.15 is certified copy of gift deed dtd: 17.10.2015,
Ex.P.16 is certified copy of order sheet C.Misc.no.246/2015,
Ex.P.17 is certified copy of C.Misc.no.246/2015, Ex.P.18 is  13  C.Misc. 130/2017 'B' extract, Ex.P.19 is school receipts, Ex.P.20 is certified copy of order sheet in CC no.481/2015, Ex.P.21 is certified copy of FIR, Ex.P.22 is certified copy order sheet, Ex.P.23 is certified copy of charge sheet in CC 5836/2015, Ex.P.24 is copy of FIR in Cr.no.158/2014 and Ex.P.25 is birth certificate. The respondent no.1 examined as RW.1 and got exhibited as Exs.R.1 to 3. Ex.R.1 is copies of petition and order sheet in OS no.6966/2016, Ex.R.2 is copy of petition in OS no.297/2017 and Ex.R.3 is vehicle particulars. 
 19. Heard both sides and perused the materials placed on record. 
 20. The points that arise for consideration are:- 
 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  protection order relief as contemplated  under Sec.18 of PWDV Act?
 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  monetary relief as contemplated under Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
10 Sec.20 of PWDV Act? 
 3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation relief as contemplated  under Sec.22 of PWDV Act?
 14  C.Misc. 130/2017  4. What order? 
 21. The findings to the above points are as follows:-
 Point Nos.1 to 3 - In the Negative  Point No.4 - As per Final Order, for the  following:-
 REASONS  22. Reasoning on Point Nos.1 to 3: Since these points are interconnected with each other and requires common appreciation of evidence, hence to avoid repetition of facts all the points are taken together for common consideration. 
 23. The case of the petitioner is that the respondent has given mental and physical harassment by demanding additional dowry and for grant of permanent accommodation. The petitioner has sought for various reliefs which are fallen U/sec. 18, 20 and 22 of DV Act.
 24. In the affidavit filed by the petitioner along with petition she has stated that the averments made in the petition are all true and correct. The petitioner has stated that she was subjected to verbal and emotional abuse and  15  C.Misc. 130/2017 she was insulted for not bringing additional dowry and she was also subjected to economic violence by not providing Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
11 money for maintaining herself. Further, the petitioner stated that the respondents were always tortured the petitioner both mentally and physically by abusing her in filthy language without any reason. Further, the contention of the petitioner is that the respondents have always abusing the petitioner and they totally changed the atmosphere of matrimonial home and they have stopped to give respect to the petitioner and they have not talked with her properly. 
 25. Further, the respondent used to assault the petitioner and caused mental and physical torture. Further the petitioner has caused lot of mental stress and strain in her mind and also the minor child. Further, the respondent no.1 has stopped talking with the petitioner and he has totally neglected her and her minor female child and also the respondents have beaten the petitioner for several times to bring additional dowry. But, in the objections, the  16  C.Misc. 130/2017 respondent no.1 had denied all allegations made by the petitioner. Further, the respondent stated that the petitioner herself has given torture to the respondent no.1. Further, he stated that their marriage was love marriage, and it was performed at the temple at the cost of respondent no.1. 
Further, he denied his income as stated by the petitioner in the petition and the respondent no.1 don't have any source of income to pay damages and maintenance to the Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
12 petitioner. Further he has taken the contention that the she is earning and she is capable to take care herself as such she is not facing any financial problems as stated in her petition. 
 26. Further on perusal of the petition, it can be seen that the petitioner and respondent no.1 are living in shared household, at that time and at that time the respondents have harassed the petitioner emotionally and mentally by not taking care of her. On the other hand, the respondent no.1 has also filed objections by denying the allegations of the petitioner leveled against him. Thereafter, also the  17  C.Misc. 130/2017 respondent had looked after the petitioner with fulfilling her all necessities with love and affection. 
 27. No doubt, as per Sec.3 of DV Act, if at all the respondent commits any domestic violence as above pleaded is fully established by the petitioner then definitely the petitioner will be entitled for an order of residential orders as per Sec.19 of DV Act and mandatory reliefs as contemplated under Sec.20 of the Act. 
 28 . In the case on hand, it is the case of the petitioner that she is residing along with the respondent no.1 after the marriage in the shared house. When in the respondents have given mental and emotional torture to bring additional Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
13 dowry and also he neglected the petitioner for not bringing sufficient dowry. 
 29 . On perusal of the pleadings as well as evidence of both sides, it appears that there is no such domestic violence caused by the respondents against the petitioner. 
Further, it appears that the petitioner herself has left the  18  C.Misc. 130/2017 matrimonial home. With regard to the possession of mandatory reliefs as contemplated under Sec.20, it becomes just and necessary for the petitioner to establish the same. 
 30. The fact that both petitioner and the respondent no.1 are wife and husband is not in dispute. When the petitioner has let in evidence she has stated that subsequent to marriage, she is residing along with the respondents in the shared household, in their the respondents intentionally neglected the petitioner by demanding additional dowry as well as neglected the petitioner. The said contention had been categorically denied by the respondent no.1. Further,
he stated that without any reason the petitioner has left the company of the respondent no.1 and residing along with her mother and sister by blackmailing the respondent no.1 for money. 
 31. On the other hand, after service of notice, the respondent no.1 appeared before the court by filing vakalath from his counsel along with permission application and filed Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
14  19  C.Misc. 130/2017 objections to the main petition by denying all averments pleaded by the petitioner in her petition. 
 32. The petitioner examined herself as PW-1 by filing affidavit of examination-in-chief. In the said examination-in- chief, she reiterated the averments of the petition. The counsel for the respondent has cross examined the PW.1. In the cross examination, she admitted that the marriage between the petitioner and respondent no.1 was love marriage and there was no any video or photos had been taken at the time of marriage. Further, she admits that she has not furnished any documents regarding any income of the respondent. Further, she admits that the respondent was taken care of the petitioner. Further during the course of cross examination, she stated that she has not mentioned the date on which the respondent was harassed the petitioner mentally and physically. It seems that there was no any domestic violence caused by the respondents towards the petitioner as admitted by her. 
 20  C.Misc. 130/2017  33. On the other hand, the respondent himself examined as RW.1 by filing affidavit in lieu of examination- in-chief and reiterated the averments of his objections. After giving sufficient opportunity the petitioner has not cross examined RW.1. 
Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
15  34. On going through the oral and documentary evidence of both parties, it clear that there is no any domestic violence caused by the respondents towards the petitioner. Further, she is utterly fails to prove her case by oral and documentary evidence. 
 35. On perusal of the entire pleadings and documents and oral testimony of the petitioner, it is crystal clear that the petitioner is legally wedded wife of respondent no.1 and both are living in the shared house under same roof. 
Further, it is clear that the respondents have not given any harassment mentally and physically to the petitioner by demanding additional dowry. 
 36. It is undisputed that on the date of filing the  21  C.Misc. 130/2017 petitioner was legal wedded wife of respondent no.1. 
Further, the respondent in his objections stated that she is having sufficient income to lead her life. To this effect the respondent has not furnished any single document to show that she is having sufficient income. But, during the course of cross examination, the petitioner herself admitted that the respondent no.1 was not looking care of the petitioner. Mere admission is very clear that the respondents have not caused any domestic violence against the petitioner as alleged by the petitioner in her petition. 
Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
16  37. Further, the petitioner is failed to prove the allegations which are made by her in the petition as well as in examination in chief in respect of domestic violence caused by the respondents u/sec. 3 of PWDV Act. 
 The Section 3 in The Protection of Women from Domestic  Violence Act, 2005 reads as under;
Sec. 3. Definition of domestic violence.--
 For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or  commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute  domestic violence in case it.
 (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb  22  C.Misc. 130/2017  or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved  person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse,
 sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic  abuse; or  (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved  person with a view to coerce her or any other person related  to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other  property or valuable security; or  (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any  person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a)
 or clause (b); or  (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or  mental, to the aggrieved person. 
 38. On careful perusal of the above section, it is clear that in this case, the respondents have not committed any domestic violence against the petitioner as explained above. On discussing above, if the respondents have not committed any domestic violence against the petitioner,
as contemplated u/sec. 3 of PWDV Act, the petitioner is not entitled for any of the reliefs as prayed by her in the petition. Hence, this court answer these point nos.1 to 3 in the the negative. 
 39. Point No.4: In view of the findings on the above point nos.1 to 3 and the reasons stated therein, this court proceed to pass the following: -
Smt. Shwetha M vs Umesh N on 18 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160751283/
17  ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/sec. 12 of the Protection of Women from C.Misc. 130/2017 Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is hereby dismissed. 
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 18th day of May 2024). 
(Kusuma. V) MMTC-III, Bengaluru.
